candidate_briefs.capability: Check sampled one/two-port Touchstone S-matrix gain with an explicit singular-value report.
candidate_briefs.user: RF engineers reviewing a small exported network capture before model use.
candidate_briefs.pain: Element magnitudes alone can hide coupled gain; reviewers need the worst sampled matrix and the exact tolerance convention.
candidate_briefs.expected: The example intentionally exits 1: sample 0 passes, sample 1 has maximum singular value 1.4 and power gain 1.96.
candidate_briefs.contract: ASCII Touchstone 1.0 subset, one or two ports explicitly declared with --ports. A single option line explicitly specifies frequency units, S, RI/MA/DB and shared positive real R. Two-port order is S11,S21,S12,S22. The largest eigenvalue of S^H S gives power gain; the square root must be at most 1+tolerance (default 1e-9). Reciprocity is informational, not a passivity requirement. Continuations are supported; frequency must strictly increase and may start at zero.
candidate_briefs.limits: 1 MiB, 4096 samples, numeric token length64, frequency<=1e15 Hz, shared R<=1e6 ohms, RI components/MA magnitudes<=1000, DB -600..60, MA/DB angles<=360000 degrees. Tolerance0..0.001. No Touchstone2 keywords, noise records, per-port/complex reference, impedance/gamma/modal annotations, renormalization, interpolation, causality or uncertainty assessment. Passing sampled data is not physical-device certification.
candidate_briefs.acceptance: Recover coupled gain missed by per-column checks, lossless through and passive nonreciprocal networks; RI/MA/DB agreement; reject malformed options, row counts and frequency order.
candidate_briefs.notes: Qucs-S and Qucs provide circuit simulation and Touchstone components. Scikit-rf already implements passivity/dissipation-matrix tests and much broader network analysis. Its per-port reference issues informed our explicit common-real-reference limit; they are not verified requests for this product. No missing competitor capability is claimed.
candidate_briefs.overlap: All193 owned repositories were compared. No existing RF S-parameter matrix inspector was found. General numeric or evidence tools do not implement this physical-format contract.

candidate_briefs.capability: Explain Intel HEX sparse address coverage, gaps, entry context and every overlapping write without flashing.
candidate_briefs.user: Firmware maintainers reviewing a HEX handoff before device programming.
candidate_briefs.pain: A checksum-valid image can still contain contradictory writes or sparse holes; choosing a last writer hides evidence.
candidate_briefs.expected: Exit 0: six unique bytes occupy two ranges at 0x08000000..04 and 0x08000008..0A; the interior gap is four bytes. No hole is filled.
candidate_briefs.contract: ASCII Intel HEX records00/01/02/03/04/05 with actual byte count and checksum validation. Segment and linear base changes affect subsequent records. Ranges use exclusive ends. All overlaps, including identical repeats, are findings; conflicting values have no selected winner. The unambiguous sparse-map SHA256 is domain-separated and hashes sorted four-byte big-endian address plus byte, excluding conflicting cells. Entry records are unique; raw numerical coverage is checked without CPU/A20/Thumb interpretation. EOF is mandatory and final.
candidate_briefs.limits: 1 MiB,8192 records,262144 data-byte events,32-bit address space. No record may wrap its16-bit offset. Overlap evidence is capped at256 addresses with an omitted count. Gaps are informational. No conversion, winner policy, filling, binary output, flashing or hardware verification.
candidate_briefs.acceptance: Reproduce mode changes, sparse gaps, checksum errors, identical/conflicting overlaps, address-sensitive hashes, uncovered entries and overflow rejection.
candidate_briefs.notes: IntelHex and bincopy already parse, merge and convert firmware images; arkku/ihex is a compact C reader/writer. Related overlap and fill discussions are adjacent context, not proof of a current defect. Our report deliberately avoids merge precedence and fill policy.
candidate_briefs.overlap: This is Intel HEX record addressing and contradictory-write evidence, distinct from the owned generic hexadecimal/text tooling. It is not a renamed formatter or a flasher wrapper.

candidate_briefs.capability: Report per-layer two-dimensional LINE/CIRCLE/ARC bounds with explicit geometric evidence.
candidate_briefs.user: CAD export maintainers checking a small planar model-space DXF.
candidate_briefs.pain: A whole-drawing bounding box does not explain which layer/entity caused an extent, especially on an arc crossing zero degrees.
candidate_briefs.expected: Exit 0: cut layer bounds are [-2,0,3,4]; reference circle bounds are [9,9,11,11]. Three entities on two layers.
candidate_briefs.contract: ASCII DXF with one ENTITIES section and complete section/EOF structure. Only LINE,CIRCLE,ARC in model space with zero Z/thickness and default extrusion. Arc sweeps are counterclockwise, normalized modulo360 and include endpoints plus cardinal extrema. Full/zero-turn arcs are rejected: use CIRCLE. All entities, including invisible ones, contribute raw geometry. Per-layer counts, bounds and approximate total lengths retain entity evidence; zero-length LINE is an exit1 finding.
candidate_briefs.limits: 2 MiB,50000 code/value pairs,10000 entities,256 layers,128-character layer names,1024-character tag values; finite coordinate/angle absolute magnitude<=1e9. Other sections are counted and ignored. Unsupported entities, transforms, duplicate geometry fields, layouts and missing coordinates fail explicitly. No blocks, polylines, text, clipping, units conversion, repair or manufacturing certificate. Bounds/lengths use floating point.
candidate_briefs.acceptance: Correct line/circle/cardinal arc extents,350-to10-degree sweep and layer unions; reject3D, nondefault extrusion, inserts, malformed sections and duplicate geometry tags.
candidate_briefs.notes: LibreCAD is a complete CAD application. Ezdxf already computes bounding boxes across far broader entity types, including transforms and curves. Libdxfrw provides broad DXF/DWG IO. This smaller strict report is a narrower interface, not an absent competitor feature.
candidate_briefs.overlap: The owned OBJ island audit analyzes triangle edge topology in3D. This tool analyzes different file semantics, layer identities and planar primitive bounds; no shared product was subdivided.

candidate_briefs.capability: Explain MIDI key release, CC64 sustain release and exact tempo-derived held-note intervals.
candidate_briefs.user: Music editors investigating timing in a small Standard MIDI File.
candidate_briefs.pain: Note-off time and sustain release differ; ambiguous simultaneous cross-track events should remain visible.
candidate_briefs.expected: Generator creates a new invented MIDI file and refuses overwrite. The report exits0: key-off tick480, CC64 release tick960, held time1000000 microseconds and peak one held voice.
candidate_briefs.contract: Binary SMF formats0/1 with PPQ timing. Running channel status is cleared by meta/sysex. Format1 tempo must be in track0; default is500000 microseconds/quarter. Tempo integration uses exact rational arithmetic; microseconds are integer or numerator/denominator strings. CC64>=64 holds released keys until pedal up. Pedal state is per channel. Events serialize by tick,track,event index; same-channel simultaneous events across tracks are flagged. Unmatched offs and capture-end closures are findings, never fabricated observed releases. Re-striking a pitch while a prior voice is pedal-held is supported; overlapping key-down of identical channel/pitch is refused.
candidate_briefs.limits: 1 MiB,16 tracks,50000 events,20000 notes,maximum tick1e9,PPQ1..32767. Four-byte VLQ maximum. No format2/SMPTE, audible synthesis, other-controller interpretation or physical sounding-duration claims. Channel-mode/reset/all-notes-off controllers are rejected. Other meta/channel events and sysex are counted/ignored. Findings cap512, cross-track evidence256.
candidate_briefs.acceptance: Correct key/pedal release distinction, channel separation, tempo changes/rational timing, running status, incomplete captures and ambiguous ordering; reject malformed chunks/VLQs and unsupported timing.
candidate_briefs.notes: Mido already provides full SMF IO. Pretty-midi already has pedal-aware piano-roll processing; Tonejs/Midi already exposes sustain controls. This event evidence view is not the first sustain feature and does not replace these broader libraries.
candidate_briefs.overlap: The owned CUE/WAVE sample plan partitions source audio frames; PGN clock tooling handles chess labels. This project reconstructs binary musical note/controller state and tempo time, a distinct capability.

candidate_briefs.capability: Audit dBASE III binary table structure and active/deleted cell quality without coercing numeric data.
candidate_briefs.user: Legacy GIS/data ingestion maintainers reviewing a small DBF before migration.
candidate_briefs.pain: Silent float conversion, deletion filtering and cleanup can obscure malformed dates or decimal representations.
candidate_briefs.query: DBF; spreadsheet parser plus documented reference follow
candidate_briefs.expected: Generator creates a new invented DBF and refuses overwrite. Exit0: two active records sum exactly to0.30; one deleted record separately sums to9.99. A valid leap-day date is retained.
candidate_briefs.contract: Binary plain dBASE III version03 only. Validate header/descriptor terminator, unique ASCII identifier field names, record width/count, deletion flags and optional single EOF byte. C,N,D,L fields only. Active and deleted rows have separate counts and numeric aggregates. Numeric values use exact decimal arithmetic; no exponents, commas, asterisk cleanup or silent rounding. Excess fractional digits, invalid calendar dates/logicals and character control bytes are findings. Blank and zero-date fields are missing. Character cells remain raw bytes: no codepage guessing or data conversion.
candidate_briefs.limits: 4 MiB,20000 records,128 fields,field names1..10 identifier characters. C width1..254; N width1..20 with decimals<=width-2; D8; L1. No memo/FoxPro/extensions, indexes, encoding conversion, table writes or business-metric interpretation. First512 cell findings identify row/field/reason without raw cell values; aggregates/field names can still be sensitive.
candidate_briefs.acceptance: Exact0.1+0.2=.30, separate deleted rows, leap dates, invalid decimals/logicals, count/width/terminator errors, unsupported types and trailing byte rejection.
candidate_briefs.notes: SheetJS is a broad spreadsheet conversion toolkit with DBF support; it was found by following the archived SheetJS/j project reference, not as the top result of the spreadsheet-parser query. SheetJS/j is archived historical context, not a maintained alternative. Dbfread already parses active/deleted records, and dbf/infused-dbf support broader DBF workflows. Selected dbfread parsing code informed our explicit refusal to coerce comma/asterisk representations. Historical date/precision issues are adjacent evidence, not verified demand for our product.
candidate_briefs.overlap: No owned DBF binary table inspector was found among193 repositories. This is not another CSV/SQLite formatter: it validates dBASE descriptors, deletion semantics and fixed-width cell representation.
